headline: Society of Apartment Complex Residents Declares Right to 'Self-Determination' After Chairman Bans Curd Rice in Clubhouse
body:
The residents of Block C of the Shanti Enclave apartment complex have officially declared their right to 'self-determination,' citing the management committee’s unilateral and 'deeply oppressive' decision to prohibit curd rice at all clubhouse social gatherings. The declaration, drafted on the back of a grocery delivery receipt, asserts that the block is now a sovereign entity with full autonomy over its catering and condiment selections.

"For too long, we have lived under the tyranny of the 'Continental-Only' snack policy," said Rajesh Iyer, a self-appointed spokesperson for the breakaway bloc who was seen installing a makeshift border post near the elevator. "When the Chairman told us that curd rice was 'too messy' for the carpet, he didn't realize he was trampling on our fundamental right to comfort food. We aren’t just a residential wing anymore; we are a culinary republic."

Management committee members expressed confusion at the sudden geopolitical shift, noting that the clubhouse rules were intended to prevent spills during the annual society tambola night. "We haven't been served a formal secession notice, just a very long, very heated WhatsApp thread," said the Society President, who requested anonymity for fear of having his parking spot blockaded. "We are currently attempting to negotiate a peaceful resolution involving a compromise on potato chips, but the splinter group is currently demanding total independence and a dedicated fridge for their pickles."
caption: The struggle for curd rice autonomy continues as residents of Block C refuse to recognize the authority of the Clubhouse Management Committee. Is your society also on the brink of a snack-based civil war? (satire) #SocietyLife #Independence #CurdRice
igHook: Would you declare independence from your apartment society over a catering dispute?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a beige plastic boundary rope stretched across a carpeted corridor, with a hand-written sign attached that says 'Border Crossing - No Entry Without Pickle'.

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 3 wins by grounding the absurd concept of sovereignty in a highly relatable and specific culinary grievance ('curd rice being too messy'), which feels much more affectionate and human than the other repetitive RWA/secession tropes. It avoids the AI 'slop' tendency by grounding the joke in a specific, vivid scene (the pickle fridge demand) rather than just stating the premise.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article is a harmless, satirical take on trivial apartment complex politics and internal bylaws. It does not name real public or private individuals, does not target protected groups, and the image prompt describes a generic, anonymous scene.
